q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a sanitary napkin?
title: Sanitary napkin carbon footprint per pad
short: Weigh one pad's fluff pulp, superabsorbent polymer, nonwoven top sheet, PE back sheet, adhesive and wrapper, apply supplier or database factors, and add machine electricity per pad. Divide by pads made. Materials are usually most of the total; compostable materials change the end-of-life picture.
audience: Sanitary pad makers, including SHG and MSME units

ul: Fluff pulp or cotton or banana fibre core.
Superabsorbent polymer: high per kg, small in quantity.
Nonwoven top sheet, PE back sheet, release paper and hot-melt adhesive.
Pad machine and core forming electricity.
Semi-automatic units: count each machine's motor hours.

p: Used pads are mostly landfilled or incinerated. If you include end of life, state the route; do not claim compostability without a test standard behind it.

example.title: Worked example: pad unit per pad (one month)
lines: Plant total: 5,680 / 2,000,000 = 0.0028 kg CO2 per pad
Add pulp, SAP, sheets, adhesive and wrappers for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
